title: Pattern editor closes and discards edits when the save fails
body:
## Summary
PatternEditor calls onDone() after updatePattern() whatever the outcome, and the store swallows the failure, so a failed save closes the editor and throws the operator's text away.

## Description
src/components/modules/evaluator/PatternLibraryView/PatternEditor.tsx:18-22 awaits updatePattern then always runs setSaving(false); onDone(). src/stores/patternLibraryStore.ts:232-247 catches the error, sets the shared `error` and resolves void, so the caller cannot tell success from failure. Fixed looks like: updatePattern returns boolean (or Result), and PatternEditor stays open with its text and an inline error on false. The store is outside this context's paths (veto 1), hence Lane B.

## Flow
- Expand a pattern card, click Edit, change the description
- Save while the API fails (DB locked, 500)
- Observed: editor closes, the edit is gone, a generic FetchError appears on the tab

## Expected impact
An operator correcting a mined pattern no longer loses the correction on a transient failure. Could break: any other caller relying on updatePattern resolving void (grep shows PatternEditor is the only one).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - a failed save keeps the edit
Before: failed save -> editor closed, 0 of 1 edits preserved (code read, PatternEditor.tsx:20-22)
After: predicted 1 of 1 preserved
Method: simulation - the store file is outside this round's paths, so the change could not be built and measured here
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: component test: stub fetch to return {success:false} for action=update, edit the description, click Save Changes, assert the textarea is still rendered with the edited text

title: Pattern library shares one error field across unrelated loads
body:
## Summary
Anti-pattern load, verify, pin and author failures all write patternLibraryStore.error, which the Patterns tab renders as a load FetchError whose Retry refetches the dashboard.

## Description
src/stores/patternLibraryStore.ts:257 (fetchAntiPatterns), :210 (verify), :228 (pin), :190 (author) set the same `error` the dashboard load uses. src/components/modules/evaluator/PatternLibraryView/index.tsx renders it on the Patterns tab as FetchError(onRetry=fetchDashboard). A failed anti-pattern fetch after a good dashboard load therefore shows 'Failed to load anti-patterns' above a correctly loaded pattern list, and Retry re-runs the wrong request. Fixed: per-operation error slots (loadError / mutationError / antiPatternError) rendered where they belong.

## Flow
- Dashboard loads fine, its piggybacked fetchAntiPatterns fails
- Patterns tab shows a load-failure banner over a full list
- Retry refetches the dashboard, not the anti-patterns

## Expected impact
Error copy matches the operation that failed. Could break: AntiPatternList if it reads `error`.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - errors are attributed to the operation that failed
Before: 4 operations share 1 error slot (store read)
After: predicted 1 slot per surface
Method: simulation - store is out of this round's paths
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: component test: dashboard ok, action=anti-patterns returns {success:false}; assert the Patterns tab shows no FetchError

title: Pattern module filter lists only the top 10 modules
body:
## Summary
The Patterns tab's module filter options come from the dashboard's topModules, which getPatternDashboard caps at 10, so patterns of an 11th module cannot be filtered to.

## Description
src/components/modules/evaluator/PatternLibraryView/index.tsx builds the module <select> from topModules; src/lib/pattern-library-db.ts getPatternDashboard sorts moduleCounts and slices to 10. The category filter, by contrast, lists every category (no cap) - two lists of one kind of facet, only one complete. Fixed: the dashboard returns the full module facet (or a separate `modules` field) and the filter uses it; topModules stays a ranking.

## Flow
- Library holds patterns for 11+ modules
- Open the module filter
- Observed: the least-populated module is missing

## Expected impact
Every module that has patterns is filterable. Could break: nothing visible; the select grows.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - every module with patterns is filterable
Before: min(10, modules) options (code read)
After: all modules with patterns
Method: simulation - fix sits in pattern-library-db.ts (out of paths)
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
src/lib/pattern-library-db.ts getPatternDashboard: .sort((a, b) => b.patternCount - a.patternCount).slice(0, 10)
src/components/modules/evaluator/PatternLibraryView/index.tsx: const moduleIds = useMemo(() => topModules.map((m) => m.moduleId), [topModules]);
instrument: db test over a temp DB with patterns in 11 modules: dashboard module facet length 11; component test option count 12 incl. 'All modules'

title: Asset oracle rescan blanks the view, hiding the remedy outcome
body:
## Summary
runAnalysis clears the result before scanning, so the rescan a remedy triggers removes the violations list and the RemedyBar 'running' line for the whole scan.

## Description
src/components/modules/evaluator/AssetCodeOracleView/useAssetCodeOracle.ts:73 setResult(null) at the start of every run; index.tsx renders nothing from `result` while loading. A remedy completion calls runAnalysis (:116), so the user who clicked 'Fix N naming mismatches' watches the whole surface vanish to a spinner-less empty card. Fixed: keep the previous result visible (dimmed / marked 'rescanning') until the new one lands.

## Flow
- Run Analysis, click a Fix button
- CLI completes -> onComplete -> runAnalysis
- Observed: result=null; list, diff banner and RemedyBar disappear until three filesystem calls return

## Expected impact
Operators keep context during a rescan. Could break: a stale list could be acted on mid-scan; disable Fix buttons while loading.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the remedy outcome stays on screen through the rescan
Before: 0 violation rows rendered while the rescan is pending (code read :73)
After: predicted prior rows kept, marked rescanning
Method: simulation - a UX choice (stale-while-loading vs blank) best decided by an A/B on the component test
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: component test: hold the scan-assets fetch on a deferred promise after onComplete(true); assert violation rows are still present and a 'rescanning' status is shown

title: Deep-eval git attribution failures are swallowed silently
body:
## Summary
A failing /api/evaluator/git-attribution call is caught with an empty catch, so NEW findings lose their 'Introduced in' line with no log and no reason.

## Description
src/components/modules/evaluator/DeepEvalResults/useDeepEvalResults.ts:190 `catch { // Attribution is optional }`. Optional is fine; silent is not - a broken git path, a wrong projectPath or a route error is indistinguishable from 'no commits touched these files'. Fixed: logger.warn with the reason, and optionally an attribution-unavailable note in the regression banner.

## Flow
- Run a scan with a baseline so NEW findings exist
- git-attribution route errors
- Observed: rows show no commit, nothing logged

## Expected impact
Attribution outages become visible in logs. Could break: nothing.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - attribution failure leaves a trace
Before: 0 log lines on failure
After: 1 logger.warn
Method: simulation - not built this round (budget went to verdict-surface defects)
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
src/components/modules/evaluator/DeepEvalResults/useDeepEvalResults.ts:190  } catch {
src/components/modules/evaluator/DeepEvalResults/useDeepEvalResults.ts:191    // Attribution is optional - leave it empty if git/the route fails.
instrument: hook test: baseline + NEW finding, stub /git-attribution to reject, spy logger.warn, assert called once with the reason

title: Re-evaluate is clickable during a running scan and silently does nothing
body:
## Summary
ModuleSection's Re-evaluate button stays enabled while a deep-eval job runs, and startJob returns early on isRunning, so the click is a silent no-op.

## Description
src/components/modules/evaluator/DeepEvalResults/ModuleSection.tsx Re-evaluate button has no disabled prop; src/components/modules/evaluator/DeepEvalResults/useDeepEvalResults.ts:256 `if (isRunning || moduleIds.length === 0) return;`. The header Run button is swapped for Cancel while running, so the two entry points disagree. Fixed: thread isRunning through index.tsx -> ResultsSection -> ModuleSection and disable with a title explaining why.

## Flow
- Start a full run
- Expand a module from the previous result, click Re-evaluate
- Observed: nothing happens, no feedback

## Expected impact
No dead clicks during a scan. Could break: nothing; prop added to 3 components.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - no silent no-op button
Before: 1 enabled button that does nothing while running
After: 0
Method: simulation - 3-file prop thread, deferred past this round's budget
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: component test: render ResultsSection with isRunning=true and an expanded module; assert the Re-evaluate button is disabled

title: Single-module re-evaluation replaces the whole result view
body:
## Summary
Re-evaluating one module clears the result and renders a result that holds only that module, so every other module's findings vanish from the view.

## Description
src/components/modules/evaluator/DeepEvalResults/useDeepEvalResults.ts:257 setResult(null) then the one-module job result replaces `result` (:110). The merged baseline keeps the other modules' findings (mergeBaseline, :139) but the view does not show them. Fixed: merge the single-module result into the displayed result (replace that module's section, keep the rest, recompute totals).

## Flow
- Run a full deep eval over 8 modules
- Click Re-evaluate on one module
- Observed: the result shows 1 module; the other 7 modules' findings are gone until a full run

## Expected impact
Iterating on one module keeps the rest of the picture. Could break: totals/severity counts must be recomputed from the merged set.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - other modules' findings survive a single re-evaluation
Before: 1 of 8 module sections visible after re-evaluate (code read)
After: 8 of 8
Method: simulation - needs a merge helper and its test; M
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: hook test: full result with 2 modules applied, then handleRunSingle on one returning a 1-module result; assert activeFindings.modules length 2

title: Evaluator fixes and oracle remedies run on the ai-behavior CLI session
body:
## Summary
Deep-eval Fix and Asset-Oracle remedies dispatch through useModuleCLI with moduleId 'ai-behavior', so their sessions, analytics and any module-scoped context are filed under AI Behavior.

## Description
src/components/modules/evaluator/DeepEvalResults/useDeepEvalResults.ts:47 moduleId: 'ai-behavior'; src/components/modules/evaluator/AssetCodeOracleView/useAssetCodeOracle.ts:21 REMEDY_MODULE = 'ai-behavior' ('the evaluator's CLI precedent module'). A deep-eval fix for arpg-combat is recorded as an ai-behavior session. Which module owns an evaluator-originated fix (the finding's module, an evaluator pseudo-module, or ai-behavior) is a product decision about how session analytics are attributed.

## Flow
- Click Fix on an arpg-combat finding
- Session analytics record moduleId ai-behavior

## Expected impact
Session analytics attribute fixes to the module they changed. Could break: session reuse keys and any dashboards keyed on ai-behavior.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - fix sessions attributed to the right module
Before: 2 evaluator surfaces hard-wired to ai-behavior
After: depends on the chosen owner
Method: simulation - the owner of evaluator sessions is a direction call
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: direction
instrument: n/a - operator decides the owning module
